findings.claim: In getAuthorizationConditions for org scope, userIdsFromOrg is fetched only when teamsFromOrg.length > 0. For orgs with no child teams, org-level members' personal bookings are excluded, even though teamIds already includes orgId.

verifier.reason: In packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:154-168, teamIds always includes options.orgId, but userIdsFromOrg is only fetched when teamsFromOrg.length > 0 (line 158). Otherwise it is [], so the personal-booking clause ("isTeamBooking" = false) is never added and org members' personal bookings are left out. The patch did not touch these lines, and the legacy code at packages/features/insights/server/trpc-router.ts:88 has the same pattern.

findings.claim: The integration tests for team and org scope conditions only compare the generated Prisma.Sql structure with toEqual and never run the queries against Postgres. The ANY(...) array-parameter binding paths are therefore untested at runtime.

verifier.reason: The team and org scope tests only check the generated SQL with toEqual against `Prisma.sql` objects (insightsBooking.integration-test.ts, patch lines 76-80 and 108-119). The only test that runs a query against Postgres is the getBaseConditions test (lines 468-484), and it uses scope "user", so the `ANY(${array})` conditions in insightsBooking.ts (patch lines 479-483 and 531) are never executed in a test.

findings.claim: The hand-written InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions type flattens the zod discriminated union and makes teamId optional for all scopes. A team-scope call without teamId compiles, fails safeParse at runtime and silently returns empty results; this is also inconsistent with InsightsRoutingService's strict union type.

verifier.reason: The patch adds the flat type `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` at packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:29-34 (`scope: "user"|"org"|"team"`, `teamId?: number`) and uses it for the constructor (line 58), replacing the strict discriminated-union type. A team-scope call without teamId therefore compiles, fails `safeParse` (line 62-63), sets options to null and gets `1=0`, so it returns empty results with no error. InsightsRoutingService still uses the strict union type (insightsRouting.ts:29,52).

findings.claim: The test fixtures userEventType and userBooking are cleaned up only after the assertions, not in try/finally. A failing query or expectation leaves those rows in the integration database.

verifier.reason: In packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:445-500, userEventType and userBooking are created and then deleted at lines 494-499 after the $queryRaw and expect at 480-491, with no try/finally. A failing query or assertion skips the deletes and leaves both rows in the database.

findings.claim: In getBaseConditions(), the `else if (filterConditions)` and final `else return NOTHING_CONDITION` branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a truthy Prisma.Sql.

verifier.reason: getAuthorizationConditions() (packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:83-88) returns the result of buildAuthorizationConditions(), and every path there returns a Prisma.Sql object: NOTHING_CONDITION, Prisma.sql`...`, or the org/team builders. A Prisma.Sql object is always truthy, so the `else if (filterConditions)` and `else return NOTHING_CONDITION` branches at lines 76-80 can never run.

findings.claim: The org-scope test assertion depends on the order of ids inside ANY(...) arrays. Those ids come from repository queries (findAllByParentId, MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds) without orderBy, so the SQL-fragment equality is nondeterministic.

verifier.reason: The new org-scope assertion in insightsBooking.integration-test.ts compares fixed ids inside ANY(...) arrays, and those arrays are built in insightsBooking.ts:150-168 from team.ts:192 (findAllByParentId) and membership.ts:409 (findAllByTeamIds). Neither query has an orderBy, so row order is not guaranteed. The test it replaces made the same assumption with `in: [...]` arrays, so the patch only carried the existing flakiness over.

findings.claim: The 'Caching' describe block test was deleted, but the memoisation code it covered (cachedAuthConditions / cachedFilterConditions) remains and is now untested.

verifier.reason: The patch deletes the 'Caching' describe block from insightsBooking.integration-test.ts (patch lines 174-236). The memoisation is still in place at insightsBooking.ts:49-50 and :84-94, and no other test covers it (only insightsRouting has a Caching block).

findings.claim: buildOrgAuthorizationCondition/buildTeamAuthorizationCondition produce top-level OR expressions without outer parentheses, and getBaseConditions() returns them directly. When callers compose them with AND, operator precedence lets rows matching the first OR branch bypass additional filters.

verifier.reason: The builders do return OR expressions without outer parentheses (insightsBooking.ts:171-174 and 204-207), but getBaseConditions wraps both sides when it ANDs them (insightsBooking.ts:73). The only caller in the repo, the integration test, uses the result on its own in `WHERE ${baseConditions}` (insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:480-484), so no caller ANDs it and no rows can bypass a filter today; the risk is only for future callers.

findings.claim: The same AND/OR reduce fold is hand-written three times instead of using Prisma.join or a direct expression.

verifier.reason: The patch hand-writes the same `conditions.reduce((acc, condition, index) => index === 0 ? condition : Prisma.sql`(${acc}) AND/OR (${condition})`)` fold three times: once with AND in buildFilterConditions (change.patch:406-409) and twice with OR in buildOrgAuthorizationCondition (change.patch:486-489) and buildTeamAuthorizationCondition (change.patch:534-537). In the latter two the list has at most two items, so a direct expression or Prisma.join would be simpler.
